title: Multihop communication patterns profiling
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a focused set of experiments and observations around multihop communication patterns in our multi-GPU inference clusters. The idea: when collective or point-to-point traffic traverses multiple physical hops (NVLink -> NVSwitch -> PCIe -> NIC), we observe non-linear throughput loss and amplified tail latency compared to single-hop flows. We want to understand where stalls/queueing happen, how NCCL routing choices interact with topology, and what mitigations (scheduling, pacing, shard placement) are promising for TP/PP LLM serving workloads.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Multihop flows frequently see 20–40% lower effective bandwidth compared to single-hop flows of the same message size under realistic traffic mixes.
- Tail latency (95/99) increases disproportionately — microbursts from other jobs or host-to-host transfers amplify queuing on intermediate switches/links.
- NCCL's chosen ring/graph and fallback to host-based copies are significant contributors to variation. We observed cases where NCCL picks a host-staging route that adds an extra hop and doubles latency.
- Two practical mitigations helped in small trials: hop-aware replica placement (place TP shards to minimize hop count for dominant collectives) and light-weight packet pacing at the driver level to smooth microbursts.

Experiment design and environment:
- Hardware: 8x A100 per node for most tests; also ran 4x A100 nodes connected over InfiniBand through two leaf switches (leaf1 <-> spine <-> leaf2). Some tests on 16-GPU NVLink mesh (2 nodes, NVSwitch fabric).
- Kernel/software: CUDA 12.2, NCCL 2.18, OFED 6.0, linux 6.1, igb/mlx driver stack default. Serving runtime: local branch 'multihop-probes-2024-09' with added tracing hooks.
- Tools: nccl-tests (allreduce/allgather/bw tests), ib_write_bw, ib_read_bw, iperf3 (for NIC baseline), nvprof/nv-nsight system-wide GPU traces, perf counters for PCIe (PCIe bandwidth counters), ethtool for link settings, and our internal trace collector (trace-id -> S3).
- Workload patterns: short-message allreduce (tensor-parallel KV cache updates, ~2–64KB messages), long-message allgather (parameter sync / rollouts, ~256KB–2MB), pipelined staged transfers for pipeline-parallel (large chunked activations, ~1–8MB chunk sizes), and mixed random interleaved requests mimicking production arrival patterns with Poisson bursts.

Key experiments & observations:
1) Single-hop vs multihop bandwidth sweep (nccl-bw)
- Method: run nccl-tests bw with message sizes 1KB -> 4MB on same-node NVLink (single-hop), node-to-node with direct leaf connectivity (single-hop IB), and node-to-node crossing spine (multihop IB).
- Observations: for 8KB–64KB messages, single-hop sustained ~9.4 GB/s (per-link aggregated), multihop dropped to 5.8–7.2 GB/s depending on active flows. For >1MB messages the gap narrowed (switch buffers amortize larger packets).
- Interpretation: small-to-medium messages suffer from partial injection and switch arbitration; every extra hop adds serialization and head-of-line risks for small packets.

2) Tail-latency amplification under mixed traffic
- Method: create a background churn of short allreduces from other ranks while measuring 99th percentile latency for a target flow (8KB).
- Observations: 99p latency increased 3x on multihop paths vs 1.5x on single-hop. Trace evidence shows repeated queuing at the ingress of the spine switch and host staging retransfers when NIC congestion occurs.
- Notable: when other jobs create microbursts, NCCL sometimes re-routes future transfers via the host (pinned to CPU DMA) which creates a long tail.

3) NCCL route choices and their cost
- Method: instrumented NCCL hooks to log ring/graph selection and fallback events; correlated with nvlink/nvlink stats and PCIe counters.
- Observations: NCCL prefers GPU-direct routes but will insert host copies when certain links are saturated or when it detects asymmetric link capacity. These host copies add ~200–800 microseconds per transfer (measured for 32KB messages) compared to GPU-direct multihop.
- Actionable: expose a runtime flag to prefer GPU-direct even if it increases imbalance, or better: cost-model NCCL decisions with measured per-hop latencies.

4) Pipeline-parallel chunk scheduling sensitivity
- Method: mimic PP with a 4-stage pipeline over 8 GPUs (2 per stage), vary chunk size and injection pacing. Measure end-to-end service latency and per-chunk latency distribution.
- Observations: smaller chunk sizes reduce compute wait but dramatically increase multihop communication overhead due to frequent small transfers across the spine. Optimal chunk size shifted upward for multihop topologies vs single-node.
- Recommendation: adaptive chunk-sizing — pick chunk size based on route hop count and measured per-chunk overhead.

5) Microburst root cause analysis (PCIe translation + NIC bursts)
- Evidence: perf counters showed PCIe_tx_util spikes exactly aligned with IB driver transmit bursts; NIC driver queues emptied in flurries that matched allreduce start times from other tenants. Switch queue depth monitors show transient pressure causing dequeue starvation for longer messages.
- Mitigation candidate: introduce randomized start offsets and small byte-level pacing windows at the transport layer (e.g., 32–128us pacing bursts). We tried soft pacing (sleep/yield in user-space) and saw 10–18% 99p latency improvement for the target flow at the cost of ~3–6% throughput reduction.

Practical mitigations tested (short trials):
- Hop-aware placement: co-locate TP shards and PP adjacent stages to reduce spine crossings. Result: 15–25% tail percentiles improved for small-message allreduces.
- NCCL tuning: forcing ring-LL vs tree collective heuristics changed trade-offs — rings helped in symmetric fabrics, trees were slightly better when one link was saturated. No silver bullet; need dynamic selection.
- Soft packet pacing: smoothing start times at the application level reduced amplification of microbursts; good wins for mixed-tenant environments.
- Route-aware admission: simple admission control for background syncs (throttle non-critical allgathers during peak requests) showed strong wins in our sim.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Can we collect per-hop per-collective hardware latency telemetry end-to-end and feed back to NCCL decision logic? Confluence page linked.
- Evaluate a driver-level hardware pacing mechanism (NIC firmware capable) vs user-space pacing. What's the CPU overhead tradeoff?
- Integrate topology-aware scheduler into runtime placement decisions: add a placement cost heuristic (hop_count * estimated_per_hop_latency + contention_penalty). Need to prototype scheduler and run scale tests.
- Test on different fabrics (Mellanox vs Broadcom switches, NVSwitch partitioning) to see vendor-specific behavior.

Quick reproducibility notes (commands used):
- nccl-tests bw: MPIRUN -np 8 -H hostfile "./build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 4096 -f 2 -g 8" (example)
- IB stress: ib_write_bw -n 1000 -s 4096 -F (bi-directional)
- PCIe perf counters: sudo perf record -e pci:* -a ... (light-weight sampling)
- Trace pipeline run: ./run_pp_sim --stages 4 --chunk 512k --pacing 0|32us --trace-id T20240912-01

Logs & traces location:
- All captures for referenced runs are in s3://redwood-internal/traces/multihop-probes/2024-09/ (trace ids in linked_artifacts list).

Immediate action items:
- (Rajat) Add a lightweight hop_count estimator to the runtime placement heuristic prototype (due: 2024-10-10).
- (Ava) Run vendor switch comparison (Mellanox vs Broadcom) on 2-node multihop setup, collect 1KB-64KB sweeps (due: 2024-10-07).
- (Luis) Prototype user-space pacing utility integrated into our serving runtime (patch branch: multihop-pacing) and test CPU/throughput trade-offs.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally experimental; numbers vary by fabric and load. The goal is to identify robust, low-complexity mitigations we can ship in the short-term (placement + pacing + NCCL hinting) and to scope longer-term work (driver/firmware pacing, NCCL cost-model integration).

Appendix: quick observations (raw numbers snapshot) - testbed: 2 nodes, 4 GPUs/node crossing spine
- 8KB message, single-hop: median 120us, 99p 220us, throughput ~7.9 GB/s
- 8KB message, multihop: median 150us, 99p 670us, throughput ~5.6 GB/s
- 512KB message, single-hop: median 1.9ms, 99p 2.6ms, throughput ~10.5 GB/s
- 512KB message, multihop: median 2.1ms, 99p 3.0ms, throughput ~9.6 GB/s

If you want, I can extract a compact set of plots (bandwidth vs message size, p99 vs background intensity) and drop them in the trace bucket for review.
